headline: High: dexter’s broad network egress and shared file scratchpad can leak or misapply outputs when paired with a local-only Godot RL agent, while prompt-injection risk is low due to no documented shared channel.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: dexter has a writable scratchpad (.dexter/scratchpad/) and autonomous execution, but godot_rl_agents shows no I/O surfaces or shared channel. Without a documented bridge, prompt injection is limited to unusual manual copy/paste or external wiring, so the pair risk stays low.
conditions: IF an operator copies dexter output into godot_rl_agents prompts or configs
IF both agents are connected through a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Disable copy/paste of raw agent output into the other agent
Add a manual review step before any cross-agent transfer
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to transferred text

B_data_leakage.rationale: dexter touches financial and market data and has broad network egress plus multiple API calls, while godot_rl_agents has no network egress and no data classes touched. The main leakage path is dexter exporting sensitive context or files; the pair still creates a default exposure risk if shared workspace data is reused.
conditions: IF dexter is given financial or market files in a shared workspace
IF dexter sends those files or derived context to external APIs
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of dexter’s scratchpad
Restrict dexter API keys to non-sensitive test data
Run godot_rl_agents in a separate directory with no shared mounts
Review outbound requests from dexter before enabling live data
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: dexter has broad network egress and autonomous execution, but godot_rl_agents has no documented write, network, or concurrency surfaces. There is no evidence of overlapping mutable resources, so direct capability conflict is limited unless an operator adds shared writable state.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory or git repo
IF an operator grants godot_rl_agents write access not shown in its profile
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Avoid shared git branches or locks-free edits
Run only one writer at a time
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared artifacts

D_cascading_error.rationale: dexter can autonomously execute and call external APIs, while godot_rl_agents is a simulation-oriented agent with no documented verification or action-taking controls. If dexter’s outputs are fed into godot_rl_agents as authoritative inputs, errors can cascade into downstream decisions or training artifacts.
conditions: IF godot_rl_agents consumes dexter outputs without validation
IF dexter-generated facts are used to label, train, or steer simulations
mitigations: Require human review of dexter outputs before reuse
Add schema validation on transferred outputs
Compare dexter claims against a second source
Log provenance for every imported artifact
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks

E_compliance.rationale: dexter explicitly touches financial and market data and requests multiple external API keys, while godot_rl_agents shows no data classes or residency controls. The pair can therefore create compliance mismatch if regulated financial data is routed through dexter and then reused elsewhere; the other agent is not cited because its profile lacks residency or certification claims.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is processed through dexter
IF retention or residency requirements apply to artifacts later reused by godot_rl_agents
mitigations: Do not route regulated data through dexter
Use synthetic or anonymized datasets
Document retention and deletion rules for shared artifacts
Check API vendor terms before enabling live data
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware routing
